analyst_view.overall: RB Salzburg are 26th with 4 points and need wins, while Ararat-Armenia are last with no points after four games and lost their last European game 0-4 to AZ. Salzburg arrive after a 1-0 defeat at Austria Wien on Sunday, their first league loss of the season, with coach Danny Röhl watching from the stands through a red-card ban and Karim Konate missing a penalty. The big new fact is that top scorer Haris Tabakovic (15 goals this season, 6 in Europe) tore his meniscus on international duty and is out until January; he is not in the brief's missing list, so the numbers don't know. Salzburg are also without Boma, Kitano, Mellberg, Omoregie and Schmid. Ararat's goalkeeper João Bravim (red card) and Bruno Wilson (yellow-card ban) are out and already counted, which is why the numbers expect so many Salzburg goals.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals, 2.9 of them Salzburg's, already adding for Ararat's missing goalkeeper Bravim and defender Bruno Wilson and taking off Wilson's share of Ararat's goals. I lean lower, to about 3.3: Salzburg lose Tabakovic, their 15-goal striker, until January, and without him they drew a blank at Austria Wien with Konate missing a penalty.

corners.text: The numbers expect 8.6 corners, 5.3 for Salzburg. Losing a central striker changes who finishes moves more than how often Salzburg reach the byline, and Ararat should sit deep as the numbers already assume, so I stay at about 8.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards, already adding a little for Ararat's busy recent card count (+7%), which includes the red that ruled out Bravim. No referee is named yet and it is unclear whether Röhl's touchline ban also covers Europe; that does not change how players foul, so I stay at about 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers expect 29.7 shots, 18.8 for Salzburg, already adding for their busy recent attack (+8%). Salzburg still created enough at Austria Wien to win a penalty and have two goals ruled out, so volume should hold without Tabakovic and I stay at about 30.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target, adding for Salzburg's sharp recent finishing (+10%). I trim it slightly to about 10.0 because that accuracy came largely through Tabakovic, who is out until January; Konate and Vertessen have to carry the line now.
